Merge

object.list.contact <- list(
  Control = chat_control_fvb,
  Disease = chat_disease_fam
)
object.list.secreted <- list(
  Control = chat_control_fvb_secreted,
  Disease = chat_disease_fam_secreted
)
cellchat.contact <- mergeSpatialCellChat(
  object.list.contact,
  add.names = names(object.list.contact),
  cell.prefix = TRUE
)
## Warning in mergeSpatialCellChat(object.list.contact, add.names =

Part I: Identify altered interactions and cell populations

Compare the total number of interactions and interaction strength contact

  cellchat.contact,
  show.legend = FALSE,
  group = c(1, 2)
)

gg2_contact <- compareInteractions(
  cellchat.contact,
  show.legend = FALSE,
  group = c(1, 2),
  measure = "weight"
)

Compare the major sources and targets in a 2D space (A) Identify cell populations with significant changes in sending or receiving signals Contact

num.link.contact <- sapply(
  object.list.contact,
  function(x) {
    rowSums(x@net$count) +
      colSums(x@net$count) -
      diag(x@net$count)
  }
)

weight.MinMax.contact <- c(
  min(num.link.contact),
  max(num.link.contact)
)

gg.contact.role <- list()

for (i in seq_along(object.list.contact)) {
  gg.contact.role[[i]] <- SpatialCellChat::netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(
    object.list.contact[[i]],
    title = names(object.list.contact)[i],
    weight.MinMax = weight.MinMax.contact,
    x.measure = "outdeg",
    y.measure = "indeg"
  )
}
## Signaling role analysis on the aggregated cell-cell communication network from all signaling pathways

(B) Compare outgoing (or incoming) signaling patterns associated with each cell population contact

library(ComplexHeatmap)
## Loading required package: grid
## ========================================
## ComplexHeatmap version 2.18.0
## Bioconductor page: http://bioconductor.org/packages/ComplexHeatmap/
## Github page: https://github.com/jokergoo/ComplexHeatmap
## Documentation: http://jokergoo.github.io/ComplexHeatmap-reference
## 
## If you use it in published research, please cite either one:
## - Gu, Z. Complex Heatmap Visualization. iMeta 2022.
## - Gu, Z. Complex heatmaps reveal patterns and correlations in multidimensional 
##     genomic data. Bioinformatics 2016.
## 
## 
## The new InteractiveComplexHeatmap package can directly export static 
## complex heatmaps into an interactive Shiny app with zero effort. Have a try!
## 
## This message can be suppressed by:
##   suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ComplexHeatmap))
## ========================================
library(grid)

# Use the first two datasets, following the CellChat tutorial
i <- 1
j <- 2

# Combine all identified signaling pathways from the two datasets
pathway.union.contact <- union(
  object.list.contact[[i]]@netP$pathways,
  object.list.contact[[j]]@netP$pathways
)

# Outgoing signaling

ht_contact_out_1 <- SpatialCellChat::netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(
  object.list.contact[[i]],
  pattern = "outgoing",
  signaling = pathway.union.contact,
  title = names(object.list.contact)[i],
  width = 5,
  height = 6
)

ht_contact_out_2 <- SpatialCellChat::netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(
  object.list.contact[[j]],
  pattern = "outgoing",
  signaling = pathway.union.contact,
  title = names(object.list.contact)[j],
  width = 5,
  height = 6
)

ComplexHeatmap::draw(
  ht_contact_out_1 + ht_contact_out_2,
  ht_gap = grid::unit(0.5, "cm")
)

# Incoming signaling
#There is a lack of significant incoming signal in disease so heatmap cannot be drawn

# Overall signaling
# outgoing + incoming

ht_contact_all_1 <- SpatialCellChat::netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(
  object.list.contact[[i]],
  pattern = "all",
  signaling = pathway.union.contact,
  title = names(object.list.contact)[i],
  width = 5,
  height = 6,
  color.heatmap = "OrRd"
)

ht_contact_all_2 <- SpatialCellChat::netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(
  object.list.contact[[j]],
  pattern = "all",
  signaling = pathway.union.contact,
  title = names(object.list.contact)[j],
  width = 5,
  height = 6,
  color.heatmap = "OrRd"
)

ComplexHeatmap::draw(
  ht_contact_all_1 + ht_contact_all_2,
  ht_gap = grid::unit(0.5, "cm")
)

Part III: Identify the up-gulated and down-regulated signaling ligand-receptor pairs Identify dysfunctional signaling by comparing the communication probabities contact

# Show contact LR interactions that are stronger in Disease than Control
gg1 <- CellChat::netVisual_bubble(
  cellchat.contact,
  sources.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  targets.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  comparison = c(1, 2),
  max.dataset = 2,
  title.name = "Increased signaling in Disease",
  angle.x = 45,
  remove.isolate = TRUE
)
## Comparing communications on a merged object
# Show contact LR interactions that are stronger in Control, i.e. decreased in Disease
gg2 <- CellChat::netVisual_bubble(
  cellchat.contact,
  sources.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  targets.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  comparison = c(1, 2),
  max.dataset = 1,
  title.name = "Decreased signaling in Disease",
  angle.x = 45,
  remove.isolate = TRUE
)
## Comparing communications on a merged object
gg1 + gg2

  comparison = c(1, 2),
  max.dataset = 2,
  title.name = "Increased signaling in Disease",
  angle.x = 45,
  remove.isolate = TRUE
)
## Comparing communications on a merged object
# Show contact LR interactions that are stronger in Control, i.e. decreased in Disease
gg2 <- CellChat::netVisual_bubble(
  cellchat.secreted,
  sources.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  targets.use = c("eEVT", "Endothelial"),
  comparison = c(1, 2),
  max.dataset = 1,
  title.name = "Decreased signaling in Disease",
  angle.x = 45,
  remove.isolate = TRUE
)
## Comparing communications on a merged object
gg1 + gg2

Identify dysfunctional signaling by using differential expression analysis contact

pos.dataset <- "Disease"
features.name <- paste0(pos.dataset, ".merged")

cellchat.contact <- CellChat::identifyOverExpressedGenes(
  cellchat.contact,
  group.dataset = "datasets",
  pos.dataset = pos.dataset,
  features.name = features.name,
  only.pos = FALSE,
  thresh.pc = 0.1,
  thresh.fc = 0.05,
  thresh.p = 0.05
)
## Use the joint cell labels from the merged CellChat object
# map DEA results onto inferred communications
net.contact <- CellChat::netMappingDEG(
  cellchat.contact,
  features.name = features.name
)

net.up.contact <- CellChat::subsetCommunication(
  cellchat.contact,
  net = net.contact,
  datasets = "Disease",
  ligand.logFC = 0.05,
  receptor.logFC = NULL
)

net.down.contact <- CellChat::subsetCommunication(
  cellchat.contact,
  net = net.contact,
  datasets = "Control",
  ligand.logFC = -0.05,
  receptor.logFC = NULL
)

gene.up.contact <- CellChat::extractGeneSubsetFromPair(
  net.up.contact,
  cellchat.contact
)

gene.down.contact <- CellChat::extractGeneSubsetFromPair(
  net.down.contact,
  cellchat.contact
)

secreted

pos.dataset <- "Disease"
features.name <- paste0(pos.dataset, ".merged")

# perform differential expression analysis
cellchat.secreted <- CellChat::identifyOverExpressedGenes(
  cellchat.secreted,
  group.dataset = "datasets",
  pos.dataset = pos.dataset,
  features.name = features.name,
  only.pos = FALSE,
  thresh.pc = 0.1,
  thresh.fc = 0.05,
  thresh.p = 0.05
)
## Use the joint cell labels from the merged CellChat object
# map DEG results onto inferred communications
net.secreted <- CellChat::netMappingDEG(
  cellchat.secreted,
  features.name = features.name
)

# LR pairs with upregulated ligands in Disease
net.up.secreted <- CellChat::subsetCommunication(
  cellchat.secreted,
  net = net.secreted,
  datasets = "Disease",
  ligand.logFC = 0.05,
  receptor.logFC = NULL
)

# LR pairs relatively downregulated in Disease
# i.e. higher in Control
net.down.secreted <- CellChat::subsetCommunication(
  cellchat.secreted,
  net = net.secreted,
  datasets = "Control",
  ligand.logFC = -0.05,
  receptor.logFC = NULL
)

# deconvolute signaling genes from LR pairs
gene.up.secreted <- CellChat::extractGeneSubsetFromPair(
  net.up.secreted,
  cellchat.secreted
)

gene.down.secreted <- CellChat::extractGeneSubsetFromPair(
  net.down.secreted,
  cellchat.secreted
)
